title: Running Order, Notice and Load Size on Feed and Animal Nutrition Programmes
content:
1. Orders go into the mill's running order and are run in the order of the programme's scheduling priority and then by the day they were taken.

2. An order needs the programme's notice in business days before the mill runs it, counting days the mill grinds and not counting the day the order was taken, and a medicated ration needs the longer notice its programme carries because the mill must flush the line.

3. An order must reach the programme's minimum tons, and a smaller order is taken as bagged feed instead of being refused.

4. A load is not delivered into a bin that cannot hold it, so the tons delivered are the lesser of the tons ordered and the bin's remaining capacity, and the balance stays on order.

5. The delivery charge is raised per load where the tons delivered fall under the programme's delivery minimum, and it is not raised where the load reaches it. A delivery taken outside mill hours carries the programme's after-hours charge on top.

6. Deliveries stop while the programme stands on hold or under a directive suspension, and a member who calls for feed in either case is brought back into service first.

## Judging a load

Under the Feed and Animal Nutrition Programmes, the tons that go out are decided by the bin and not by the order alone. Where the bin's remaining capacity is the smaller of the two figures, that capacity is what is delivered and the untaken tons remain on order; where the tons ordered are the smaller, the whole order goes out.

*Hypothetical.* Eighteen tons are ordered on a programme whose bin has eleven tons of room left. Eleven tons are delivered and seven stay on order. If the same bin had twenty-two tons of room, all eighteen would go out.

*Hypothetical.* The delivery charge turns on the tons delivered rather than the tons ordered. A load that goes out exactly at the programme's delivery minimum reaches it, and no delivery charge is raised; a load that goes out one tenth of a ton below it falls under, and the charge is raised for that load. Taken outside mill hours, either load carries the programme's after-hours charge as well as whatever the first test produced.

## Two counts the desk works with

The days since the last delivery on a programme are counted from the date of the most recent load through the day the matter is handled, the delivery date counting as day nought. The tons taken in the rolling year are the sum of the tons delivered on the programme over the twelve calendar months ending on the last day of the month before the day the matter is handled.
